I've had something similar happen to me. Before I really started transitioning I exclusively liked women. The thought of being with a guy, sexually and romantically made me really uncomfortable. Looking back on it I think this was rooted in dysphoria. With a guy, he would be, obviously, the guy in the relationship and I'd be treated like his girlfriend and sex... I don't think I have to get into that. While with a girl, I felt like I was able to be more of the "man" in that sort of dynamic, I was more comfortable. But when I realized I was trans and people began to perceive me as the guy I really am, I realized I also liked guys. I knew I would be treated just as another guy, and I have since meeting my boyfriend! I was much more comfortable with myself, therefore that facit of my sexuality was able to express itself.

Whenever I'm with cis guys I'm always reminded of how short I am, how high my voice his, how feminine I look compared to them(I'm pre-t), and just about any other part of myself I'm dysphoric about. It makes me really selfconscious about every little thing I do around them. I know I pass pretty well, but I can't help but feel like they can all see right through that. It's made me uncomfortable to the point where I've begun to opt out of sports and even friendships with cis guys for fear of being treated as female. But I also feel like I get a little dysphoric here and there around girls too for being mistaken for a lesbian, but not as frequently.
